primary_source.title: Quality-Diversity Evolution for Discovering Diverse Vulnerabilities in LLM Safety
primary_source.author: Subhadip Mitra
primary_source.workshop_status: paper identifies the work as an ICLR 2026 Workshop on Agents in the Wild contribution in the clean worker source; verification here uses the author primary arXiv v1 text and linked public repository

claim_checks.claim: A random manual audit of 50 responses found about 12% heuristic-judge misclassification, mostly false negatives, with no observed false positives.
claim_checks.evidence: Section 2.2 states that manual inspection of a random sample of 50 responses across all models found an estimated ~12% misclassification rate, primarily ambiguous redirections scored as refusals (false negatives), with no false positives (refusals scored as compliance) observed. The Limitations section repeats ~12% and mostly-false-negative scope.
claim_checks.scope: This is a small pooled manual sample. 'No false positives observed' is an observed sample outcome, not evidence that the underlying false-positive rate is zero. The paper does not report the class denominator needed to estimate a class-conditional false-positive rate.

claim_checks.claim: The paper supplies a calibrated class-conditional judge-error model or controlled false-positive/false-negative corruption experiment.
claim_checks.evidence: The v1 text reports the one 50-response manual audit and proposes future LLM-as-judge improvements. No confidence-interval text, inter-rater/annotator protocol, exact confusion matrix, or controlled injected corruption sweep is reported in the paper text inspected.
claim_checks.scope: Absence from the v1 text does not prove no unpublished/internal analysis exists.

claim_checks.claim: The main QD configuration was population 30, generations 30, mutation 0.3, crossover 0.7, tournament size 3 and a 6x6x6=216 archive.
claim_checks.evidence: Main setup reports population 30, generations 30, mutation 0.3, crossover 0.7, tournament size 3 and 6x6x6 bins. Appendix Table 2 clarifies generations=30 except Devstral=20.
claim_checks.scope: Do not describe all four target runs as 30 generations without the Devstral exception.

claim_checks.evidence: The Diversity section reports 16.7% (36/216) of behavior-space cells 'across all models' and 10+ unique strategy-encoding combinations per model; coverage plateaus around generation ~20.
claim_checks.scope: The 36/216 statement is presented as an across-model aggregate/summary and should not be silently treated as a per-model occupancy statistic.

claim_checks.claim: The paper's stated heuristic fitness scale is internally identical to the linked released implementation.
claim_checks.evidence: Section 2.2 and Algorithm 1 describe heuristic outputs {0.0,0.4,1.0} with 1.0=compliance, yet Appendix Table 2 lists fitness bands {0.0,0.4,0.8,1.0} and the main results use 0.8 as successful frontier-model fitness. In the linked public repository snapshot inspected (commit 90c190202f52bad0c0d8c84fe47a9be2f1219253), HeuristicJudge assigns 0.0 to refusal, 0.8 to detected compliance and 0.4 otherwise. The repository also contains a separate LLMJudge path.
claim_checks.scope: The inspected repository snapshot is public author-linked artifact evidence, but without an experiment-manifest commit pin it should not be assumed to be the exact immutable code snapshot that generated every paper result. The discrepancy is a reporting/provenance issue, not evidence that the 50-response manual audit itself is false.

operational_interpretation.supported: Real QD/LLM evaluation can exhibit visibly asymmetric observed judge errors, so false-admit and false-reject channels should be tracked separately rather than collapsed into one scalar error rate.
not_supported: a precise class-conditional false-positive or false-negative rate
a causal estimate of how these judge errors change archive quality
transfer of the observed asymmetry to other judges, models, taxonomies or QD systems

material_correction_to_worker: C43's core observation is primary-supported, but it must be framed as a pooled n=50 observational audit rather than a calibrated error model. No false positives were observed in that sample; zero false-positive rate is not established. The paper reports no confidence interval, exact confusion matrix, annotator/inter-rater protocol or controlled corruption sweep. Also, Appendix Table 2 gives only 20 generations for Devstral, and the paper/released-code fitness scale has a provenance inconsistency: method text says compliance=1.0 while the linked HeuristicJudge snapshot scores detected compliance at 0.8 and the paper's results/appendix use a 0.8 band.
unresolved: Obtain the exact 50 manually reviewed response identities, human labels, selection seed, annotator protocol and confusion matrix if the authors release them.
Pin the exact experiment-generating repository commit/manifests to resolve the 1.0-versus-0.8 heuristic-fitness discrepancy.
Run a controlled asymmetric false-admit/false-reject corruption experiment to estimate causal archive-quality sensitivity.
